name: Keema Pav
cuisine: Mumbai (Irani cafés and street stalls; also a Ramadan sehri classic)

ingredients.name: Mutton (goat) mince (keema)
ingredients.householdMeasure: a heaped ½ cup, loosely packed

equipment: Kadai or heavy-bottomed pan (about 20 cm) with a lid
Tawa or flat pan for the pav
Wooden spoon or spatula; a potato masher or the back of the spoon to break mince lumps
Measuring spoons and a small kitchen scale (cups and spoons are given for the scale-less)
Optional: pressure cooker (1.5 L), the method in Sanjeev Kapoor's recipe: cook the mince 2–3 whistles instead of the 15 min covered simmer

steps.title: Measure the mince
steps.text: Put 125 g mutton mince in a bowl and pat it dry with paper.
steps.tip: Keep it in the fridge until step 16 so it stays safe.

steps.title: Chop the onion
steps.text: Finely chop ½ small onion (60 g).
steps.visualCue: Small even pieces, about ⅓ cup

steps.title: Chop the tomato
steps.text: Chop ½ medium tomato (60 g) into small pieces.

steps.title: Make the ginger-garlic
steps.text: Mince 1 cm ginger (5 g) and 2 garlic cloves (6 g) fine, or crush them in a mortar.

steps.title: Chop the chilli
steps.text: Chop 1 green chilli (4 g).
steps.tip: Remove the seeds for less heat.

steps.title: Measure the peas
steps.text: Put 30 g peas (2 tbsp) in a small bowl; if frozen, rinse under warm water.

steps.title: Chop the coriander
steps.text: Chop 1 tbsp (5 g) coriander leaves.

steps.title: Prepare the serving onion and lemon
steps.text: Slice 20 g onion into thin rings and cut a ¼ lemon wedge (keep 1 tsp of juice for step 20).
steps.videoShot: Onion rings and lemon on a plate.

steps.title: Mix the powders
steps.text: In a small bowl, put ¼ tsp (0.5 g) turmeric, ¾ tsp (2 g) red chilli powder and 1 tsp (3 g) coriander powder.
steps.visualCue: Three colours of powder side by side

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Put the kadai on medium heat and add 2 tsp (10 g) oil.

steps.title: Temper the whole spices
steps.text: Add 1 bay leaf, 1 cm cinnamon, 2 cloves and 1 crushed cardamom pod.
steps.visualCue: Strong sweet aroma; cloves puff slightly

steps.title: Brown the onion
steps.text: Add the chopped onion (60 g) and cook, stirring every minute.
steps.tip: If it browns too fast, lower the heat and add 1 tbsp water.
steps.visualCue: Soft, then deep golden brown at the edges; sweet smell
steps.videoShot: Onion turning golden in the oil.

steps.title: Add ginger, garlic and chilli
steps.text: Stir in the ginger-garlic and the chilli.
steps.visualCue: Raw garlic smell goes; mixture sizzles

steps.title: Cook the tomato
steps.text: Add the chopped tomato and 2.5 g salt; cook, mashing with the spoon.
steps.visualCue: Tomato breaks down to a thick paste; oil separates at the edges

steps.title: Add the powders
steps.text: Lower the heat, add the bowl of powders and 30 ml (2 tbsp) water; stir.
steps.tip: The water stops the powders burning.
steps.visualCue: Deep red-brown paste, no dry powder smell

steps.title: Add the mince
steps.text: Turn the heat to medium-high, add the 125 g mince, break up lumps with the spoon and stir.
steps.visualCue: Colour changes from pink to grey-brown; no large lumps; juices reduce
steps.videoShot: Mince breaking apart in the masala.

steps.title: Add water and peas
steps.text: Add 50 ml water and the 30 g peas; stir and bring to a gentle boil.

steps.title: Simmer covered
steps.text: Lower to low heat, cover and cook, stirring twice.
steps.tip: If it dries out before the mince is soft, add 2 tbsp hot water.
steps.visualCue: Mince is tender (a piece crumbles between spoon and pan); thick gravy
steps.cameraCheck: The keema with a spoonful lifted

steps.title: Dry it down
steps.text: Remove the lid and cook on medium heat, stirring, until thick.
steps.visualCue: Spoon leaves a trail; oil shimmers on top; no watery pool
steps.videoShot: A spoon dragged through the keema leaving a trail.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Switch off the heat, stir in ½ tsp (1 g) garam masala, half the coriander and 1 tsp lemon juice.
steps.tip: Spoon off any pool of oil on top before serving if you want it lighter (not counted in section 5).

steps.title: Rest it
steps.text: Leave the keema covered off the heat.

steps.title: Split the pav
steps.text: Cut each of the 2 pav (70 g) in half sideways, not all the way through.

steps.title: Melt the butter
steps.text: Heat the tawa on medium and melt 2 tsp (8 g) butter.

steps.title: Toast the pav
steps.text: Place the pav cut side down in the butter.
steps.visualCue: Cut sides golden and crisp-edged; buttery smell

steps.title: Plate it
steps.text: Put the keema (about 190 g) on a plate with the pav, serving onion, remaining coriander and the lemon wedge.
steps.videoShot: A slow pan over the plate.

steps.title: Squeeze lemon and eat
steps.text: Squeeze the wedge over the keema and eat at once, scooping keema into the pav.
steps.videoShot: A bite of pav loaded with keema.

reasons: high-quality protein (about 36 g), some fibre from onion and peas, and no deep frying. Points off for saturated fat (about 12 g, from mutton fat and butter), about 1,430 mg sodium and refined white pav. Restaurants usually use more oil or ghee, more salt and more butter on the pav, and often fatter mince.

researchRating.basis: keema pav is a much-loved Mumbai Irani-café classic (Curly Tales and Homegrown run "best kheema pav in Mumbai" lists; Cafe Military is known for it; Rana Safvi calls it a sehri favourite), and many recipe sites carry it (Sanjeev Kapoor, Ranveer Brar, Mrs Balbir Singh, SBS, Delicious, Olive). Points off because it is heavy and fatty, and per-recipe review counts were not visible (pages could only be seen through search snippets).

storage: Keema: fridge-safe in a closed box for up to 3 days (cool within 1 hour); freezes for up to 2 months. Reheat in a pan with 2 tbsp water on low until steaming hot all the way through, or microwave covered for 2 minutes, stirring once. Pav: best fresh; toast again when needed.
leftoverRemix: Keema paratha or keema toastie. Use cold keema as a paratha stuffing (mix with chopped coriander and a little grated cheese) or spread it between two slices of bread with cheese and grill until crisp. (Swiggy Instamart and Sanjeev Kapoor list keema pav with cheese-baked and "twist" versions.)
burnOff: about 9.9 km of running (690 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 13.8 km of brisk walking (about 2 h 45 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.).

navratri.reason: mutton, onion, garlic and wheat pav are all avoided

ekadashi.reason: meat, onion, garlic and a wheat bread are avoided

jain.reason: meat, onion, garlic and fresh ginger

ramadan.reason: use halal-sourced mutton; keema pav is a traditional sehri dish in Mumbai (Rana Safvi), but this plate is heavy and has about 1,430 mg sodium (est.), which adds to thirst during the fast

jain.reason: mutton, onion, garlic, fresh ginger; Jain rules exclude meat and root vegetables

sattvik.reason: contains onion and garlic, and meat

glutenFree.reason: the pav is wheat bread; the keema itself has no wheat (this recipe uses no hing), so serve it on gluten-free bread (see Gluten-free variant)

dairyFree.reason: toast the pav in oil instead of butter (8 g butter → 5 g oil); check that the pav is made without milk or butter, as some bakeries use them
